target_customer: Licensed clinicians and medical trainees, who use it free; revenue from partnerships with medical societies, publishers and health systems
problem: Clinicians need fast, trustworthy answers grounded in graded evidence at the point of care.
business_model: Free for clinicians; monetization via partnerships and healthcare market expansion (per Series A use of funds)

founders.name: Maxime Allouch
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, dual business and AI background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval and grading over a large literature corpus plus clinician trust requirements; standard LLM engineering with hard evaluation parts.

defensibility.rationale: Evidence grading framework and society partnerships help, but answer engines are copyable and well funded players exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from dated sources; a secondary aggregator lists OpenEvidence, Heidi Evidence and UpToDate as rivals, and Vera still raised a Series A in 2026-10.

market_need_then: Clinicians already searched literature and tools like UpToDate; the founders began with a tool for their physician parents per tech.eu headline coverage.

branding.domain_note: Original vera-health.ai redirected permanently to verahealth.ai (observed 2026-11); acquisition cost not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence and rigor: shows source, strength and limits of every answer

branding.community_and_virality: Reports 800,000 clinicians in 190 countries, and partnerships with medical societies (for example the Italian pediatric emergency society SIMEUP).

brand_strength.rationale: Many similarly named health companies (Verana Health, Veera Health, Vera Whole Health) crowd results; adoption evidence is usage driven, not brand driven.

outcome_analysis: Vera Health, a Summer 2024 company, grew to a reported 800,000 clinicians (company figure) and raised a 28.5M Series A led by Threshold Ventures in October 2026, with total funding stated as about 32M. The timing tailwind of LLM clinical search and free access for clinicians drove adoption; earlier round details are not public.
notes: Series A figure and investors appear across many outlets in search results (Fierce Healthcare, tech.eu, Digital Health News, citybiz, healthcareittoday which says 32M total); Fierce page returned 403 so tech.eu is the cited source. Optum Ventures participation appears in only one outlet and is omitted. Earlier seed: Gradient claims it led a seed (dated 2026-03 in a search snippet, page not opened), amount not public; Preqin lists a 2024-09 seed from Pioneer Fund for 'Veracity-Health Inc.', which may be a different company. Aggregators show 500K, unverified. 32M total implies about 3.5M earlier, inferred by a search summary, not stated. Competitor list left empty because only 2026 sources named rivals. Founders' technical status and employers are not stated on the YC page.
